Keywords: pre-commit hook lint format validate check staged files --no-verify bypass
Description: Run automatically before git commit. Per official docs: can be bypassed with git commit --no-verify. Ideal for running linters, formatters and fast tests on staged files to block bad commits locally. Receives no parameters.
When to Use: Enforcing code style and catching obvious errors before they enter the history
Command Example:
# .git/hooks/pre-commit (chmod +x)
#!/bin/sh
# Run ruff linter on staged Python files
STAGED=$(git diff --cached --name-only --diff-filter=ACM | grep '\.py$')
if [ -n "$STAGED" ]; then
    echo "$STAGED" | xargs ruff check --fix
    echo "$STAGED" | xargs ruff format
    echo "$STAGED" | xargs git add
fi

# Or use pre-commit framework
pip install pre-commit
pre-commit install
Gotchas: Hooks are not committed by default (.git/hooks/ is excluded). Use the pre-commit framework or lefthook to version-control and share hooks across the team.

Keywords: commit-msg hook conventional message format validate regex enforce
Description: Run after the commit message is written but before the commit is finalized. Use it to enforce message format (e.g. Conventional Commits).
When to Use: Enforcing a team commit message standard — blocks commits with non-compliant messages
Command Example:
# .git/hooks/commit-msg (chmod +x)
#!/bin/sh
MSG=$(cat "$1")
PATTERN='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|build|ci)(\(.+\))?: .{1,72}$'
if ! echo "$MSG" | grep -qE "$PATTERN"; then
    echo 'ERROR: Commit message does not follow Conventional Commits format.'
    echo 'Example: feat(auth): add JWT refresh token'
    exit 1
fi
Gotchas: The hook receives the commit message file path as $1 — read it with cat. If the script exits non-zero the commit is aborted.

Keywords: pre-push hook test run CI validate before push remote
Description: Run before git push executes. Ideal for running the test suite or build to prevent broken code from reaching the remote.
When to Use: Blocking pushes that break tests — a local CI gate before code reaches the server
Command Example:
# .git/hooks/pre-push (chmod +x)
#!/bin/sh
echo 'Running tests before push...'
python -m pytest tests/ -q --timeout=30
STATUS=$?
if [ $STATUS -ne 0 ]; then
    echo 'Tests failed — push aborted. Run pytest to see failures.'
    exit 1
fi
echo 'Tests passed. Pushing...'
Gotchas: pre-push can be bypassed with git push --no-verify. For enforcement add the same check in CI. Slow hooks will frustrate developers — keep them fast (<30s).

Keywords: pre-commit framework hooks yaml config yaml version controlled shared team
Description: .pre-commit-config.yaml stores hook configurations that are version-controlled and shared. Hooks run in isolated environments — no global tool requirements.
When to Use: Team projects that need consistent hooks across developer machines
Command Example:
# Install
pip install pre-commit

# .pre-commit-config.yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    rev: v0.3.0
    hooks:
      - id: ruff
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format

  - repo: https://github.com/pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
    rev: v4.5.0
    hooks:
      - id: trailing-whitespace
      - id: end-of-file-fixer

# Install and run
pre-commit install
pre-commit run --all-files
Gotchas: Hooks run in isolated virtualenvs — first run is slow while environments are built. Add .pre-commit-config.yaml to version control and document in README.

Keywords: post-merge hook after pull merge sync dependencies install packages
Description: Run after a successful git merge (including git pull). Useful for auto-running dependency installs when lock files change.
When to Use: Auto-installing dependencies when package lock files are updated on pull
Command Example:
# .git/hooks/post-merge (chmod +x)
#!/bin/sh
CHANGED=$(git diff-tree -r --name-only --no-commit-id ORIG_HEAD HEAD)
if echo "$CHANGED" | grep -q 'requirements.txt'; then
    echo 'requirements.txt changed — reinstalling...'
    pip install -r requirements.txt
fi
if echo "$CHANGED" | grep -q 'package-lock.json'; then
    echo 'package-lock.json changed — running npm install...'
    npm install
fi
Gotchas: post-merge does NOT run on rebase. Use post-rewrite hook for rebase-triggered installs. Avoid slow operations that block the developer workflow.

Keywords: prepare-commit-msg hook template auto-fill branch ticket jira
Description: Run before the commit message editor opens. Per official docs: this hook is NOT suppressed by --no-verify (unlike pre-commit). Takes 1-3 params: (1) commit log message file, (2) source of message (message/template/merge/squash/commit), (3) commit SHA if -c/-C/--amend. Non-zero exit aborts the commit.
When to Use: Auto-inserting a Jira/GitHub issue number from the branch name into the commit message
Command Example:
# .git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg (chmod +x)
#!/bin/sh
# Extract ticket from branch: feature/GH-123-add-cors -> GH-123
BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
TICKET=$(echo "$BRANCH" | grep -o '[A-Z]\+-[0-9]\+' | head -1)
if [ -n "$TICKET" ] && [ -z "$(head -1 $1)" ]; then
    sed -i.bak "1s/^/[$TICKET] /" "$1"
fi
Gotchas: Only fires when the user will see the editor. Not triggered by git commit -m (which skips the editor). Check $2 argument to know the message source (message/template/merge etc).

Keywords: lefthook hooks manager yaml parallel fast performance
Description: Lefthook is a fast Git hooks manager written in Go. Runs hooks in parallel. Config is version-controlled in lefthook.yml. No runtime dependencies for hook runners.
When to Use: Teams that want pre-commit-like hook management but with better performance and simpler config
Command Example:
# Install (via npm, brew, or direct binary)
npm install @arkweid/lefthook --save-dev

# lefthook.yml
pre-commit:
  parallel: true
  commands:
    lint:
      glob: '*.py'
      run: ruff check {staged_files}
    format:
      glob: '*.py'
      run: ruff format {staged_files}
pre-push:
  commands:
    tests:
      run: python -m pytest tests/ -q

lefthook install
Gotchas: Lefthook uses {staged_files} {push_files} placeholders — not available in all versions. Check the version compatibility before using.  Add lefthook.yml to .gitignore exclusions.

Keywords: post-checkout hook environment setup after branch switch virtualenv activate clone worktree
Description: Run after git checkout or git switch. Per official docs: also runs after git clone (unless --no-checkout/-n is used) and after git worktree add (unless --no-checkout). Receives 3 params: $1=old HEAD ref, $2=new HEAD ref, $3=1 for branch checkout / 0 for file checkout. Cannot affect the outcome of checkout/switch.
When to Use: Reminding developers to activate a virtualenv or run migrations after switching branches, or running setup after fresh clone
Command Example:
# .git/hooks/post-checkout (chmod +x)
#!/bin/sh
# $1=old HEAD, $2=new HEAD, $3=1 if branch checkout 0 if file checkout
# After git clone: $1=null-ref, $2=new HEAD, $3=1
if [ "$3" = '1' ]; then
    BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)
    echo "Switched to branch: $BRANCH"
    if [ -f '.env' ]; then
        echo 'Reminder: .env file exists. Activate your virtualenv.'
    fi
fi
Gotchas: post-checkout fires on file checkout too (git checkout -- file) — check $3 to distinguish. Also fires after git clone (with $1=null-ref $3=1) and after git worktree add. This hook cannot affect the outcome of checkout or switch.
